eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Helsinki's August 16 high centers on 22–23 °C because short-range ensemble forecasts from ECMWF and GFS show a tight spread around that range, driven by a weak high-pressure ridge allowing modest warm-air advection from the south while increasing afternoon cloud cover caps peak heating. Mid-August climatology for the Finnish capital places the normal daily maximum near 20 °C, so any deviation hinges on boundary-layer moisture and wind direction; current model guidance indicates light southerly flow with dew points supporting temperatures a few degrees above average. The narrow probability gap between the two leading outcomes reflects typical forecast uncertainty at the 24–36-hour horizon, where small shifts in cloud timing or frontal timing can alter the daily maximum by 1 °C. Updated high-resolution runs from the Finnish Meteorological Institute later today and tomorrow morning will provide the final inputs for resolution.
